title: Effects of Turmeric and Rosemary Extract on Oxidative Stress Markers in Goats
content: Background: Due to their versatility, goats are becoming increasingly popular as livestock on commercial farms. To obtain high productivity, the maintenance of homeostasis of their organisms is needed. The study examines the effects of mixture of turmeric-rosemary extracts on the antioxidant status of the blood of young castrated bucks. We examined the most important parameters of oxidative stress.Results: Supplementation was found to lower lipoperoxidation and increase TAC, probably due to improved neutralisation of RO species by enhanced antioxidant pathways. Despite lowering lipid peroxidation, these products can increase protein oxidation. We demonstrate that while enhancing lipid defence mechanisms may reduce lipid peroxidation, it may also increase the level of OMP, probably due to the accumulation of lipid peroxidation metabolites. The activities of SOD, GPx, and GR remained unchanged, whereas CAT activity decreased. CP, ALT, and AST remained stable, suggesting no adverse effects on key markers of liver function. Conclusions: The high antioxidant potential observed after supplementation indicates the turmeric-rosemary extract mixture elicited a favorable biochemical response; thus, the supplemented compounds effectively enhanced antioxidant defenses (by improved neutralization of ROS) without negatively affecting liver enzyme activities. Supplementing with turmeric-rosemary dry extract can significantly affect the maintenance of homeostasis and, consequently, achieve high productivity.
